issues.description: The PersonService.deletePerson method has mismatching parameter types across artifacts. The problem statement and the template expect deletePerson to take a UUID (delete by personId), and PersonResource in the solution calls personService.deletePerson(personId) (UUID). However, the solution's PersonService defines deletePerson(Person person) (taking a Person), which does not match the expected UUID parameter and causes a structural mismatch / compile error between the REST resource and the service implementation.
issues.suggestedFix: Rename or change the solution's PersonService.deletePerson(Person person) to match the expected signature deletePerson(UUID personId) (as in the template and as called by PersonResource). Update the implementation to remove by comparing person.getId() with the given UUID. This will align the service with the REST resource and the problem specification.

issues.description: The deletion API concept is inconsistently represented across artifacts: the problem statement and template expect deletion by personId (DELETE /persons/{personId}) and the template PersonService provides deletePerson(UUID personId). However, the solution's PersonService defines deletePerson(Person person) while the solution's PersonResource still calls personService.deletePerson(personId). This divergence in the method name/signature for the same conceptual operation (delete person) creates mapping confusion and can lead to compilation or integration errors and extra cognitive load for students trying to connect the REST endpoint contract with the service API.
issues.suggestedFix: Unify the deletion API by using a single, consistent method signature across artifacts. Prefer the DELETE-by-ID contract described in the problem statement and template: change the solution PersonService to expose deletePerson(UUID personId) (or alternatively adjust PersonResource to pass a Person object consistently). Align method name and parameter across PersonResource and PersonService so the REST endpoint maps clearly to the service method.
